:::{#def-argmax}
#### Argmax

Let $f : A \to \reals$ be a [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function).
The **argmax** of $f$ over $A$
is the set of inputs where $f$ takes its largest value:

$$\argmax_{x \in A} f(x) \eqdef \cb{x \in A : \all a \in A,\ f(a) \le f(x)}$$

When this set has exactly one element $\hat{x}$,
we write $\hat{x} = \argmax_{x \in A} f(x)$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-argmax}
#### An argmax with two points, and an empty one

- Let $g(x) = x^2$ on $A = \cb{-2, 0, 1, 2}$.
  The values are $g(-2) = 4$, $g(0) = 0$, $g(1) = 1$ and $g(2) = 4$,
  so the largest value is $4$ and $\argmax_{x \in A} g(x) = \cb{-2, 2}$.
  This argmax has two elements, so it is not written as a single $\hat{x}$.
- Let $f(x) = x$ on $[0, 1)$.
  As in @exm-maximum, for every input $x$ the input $\tfrac{x + 1}{2}$ has a larger value,
  so no input attains a largest value, and $\argmax_{x \in [0, 1)} f(x)$ is the
  [empty set](sets-functions.qmd#def-empty-set).

:::
